title: How we automate sales call research with AI — and how you can too
summary: Quo’s sales team uses an AI agent to research every prospect before a call. Here’s how it works and how to build a version for your business.
body_markdown:
At Quo, our account executives, or AEs, deal with back-to-back scheduled calls every day, sometimes 10 or more. With a packed schedule, there just isn’t time to do all the prep we need to do for each call. The technology exists to surface context to guide conversations more effectively. So as the Senior Sales Manager at Quo, I built an AI agent that does the prep work for AEs.


Below, I’ll walk through what’s inside our team’s call prep brief, how we built it, and how you can set up a simpler version with Claude connected to Quo. It works whether you want to prep before a[scheduled call](https://www.quo.com/blog/sales-call-planning/) or catch up after a busy day.


##


From lead form to calendar invite: Building the brief


I built the first version of the sales call research brief in Claude. Sometimes, building an AI agent can be hard if you don’t know exactly what you want. In this case, I had a clear idea of the steps each AE was doing manually to prepare for calls, like going to the prospective customer’s website, understanding what they do, etc. That made the build much faster.


When I build with AI, I follow the same process:


1. Build a first version of the agent.
2. Test it.
3. Get feedback from the team.
4. Tinker with it, ask the agent to make corrections, and test again.


I start by opening Claude and adding a prompt. I tell it, *“Here’s what I’m trying to solve for, and here’s what I’m trying to accomplish.”* From there, Claude walks me through the build.


This brief took about a week or two to finish, and the actual hands-on work took only a few hours. After that, it was mostly fine-tuning. Each round of feedback made the brief more useful to the team.


AEs say it helps them build credibility with prospects. Leads can tell we’ve researched their business and that we already work with companies like theirs. From there, the AE can show how Quo solves the problems that come up on the call.


##


What’s inside the sales call prep brief


Our agent compiles everything into one brief and adds it to the account executive’s Google Calendar invite before the call. Here’s what’s in it:


### 1. Contact, company, and rapport starters


The agent scans the prospect’s website and LinkedIn page. This gives the AE a quick read on the business and a few ways to open the conversation.


### 2. Demo request


This is what the prospect typed into our website contact form. The contact form data goes into Salesforce, and the brief pulls from there.


### 3. What we hear from similar companies


A subagent reviews our call data, which is stored in Gong. It surfaces the challenges and goals that similar companies share, along with the features they like the most. That way, the AE is ready to talk about more than what the prospect listed.


### 4. Pre-screener responses


Another AI agent emails the prospect a day before the call with a few extra questions. The answers are included in the brief and help shape the conversation.


### 5. Customer story


As most business owners know, social proof works really well. Since Quo has a lot of[customer stories](https://www.quo.com/customers) on our website, the brief suggests a relevant story the AE can bring up on the call. It also pulls in a quote or a testimonial from a real customer.


##


How to build your own version


You can build something similar by relying on tools with an MCP, or Model Context Protocol. An MCP is just a connector that lets AI tools read data from apps like Quo. If you connect[Claude](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/integrations/mcp/claude) ,[ChatGPT](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/integrations/mcp/chatgpt) , or Grok Bot to Quo with an MCP connector, you can surface customer insights from your Quo data.


You can also use the[Quo Agent](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/ai-automations/quo-agent) directly inside Quo to ask questions about your data.


A few ways to get started:


**If you’re returning a call or have one scheduled:** Before you dial, ask Claude or the Quo Agent what you already know about that person.


For example: *“I’m calling (512) 555-0142 in 10 minutes. Summarize our past calls and texts, what they said they need, and anything still open.”*


**If you take a lot of live inbound calls** , have Claude or the Quo Agent do the post-call follow-up. Try a prompt like this:


*“Review today’s inbound calls. For each caller, summarize what they need and note any past conversations with us. Then list who needs a follow-up and what they’re waiting on.”*


The next morning, you’ll start with a clear list of who to call back first.


##


How you know it’s working


In my first iteration of the call research brief, the feedback I got was that it was “interesting.” To me, that wasn’t good enough. So I asked, “How do I make this something you need on a daily basis?” My initial goal was a call brief the team was excited to use.


I kept working on it. Now our sales reps tell me they rely on the call prep brief. Recently, one of our AEs told me that details from the “what we hear from other companies” section helped her do a better job providing her clients with credible insights. I want everyone on the team to feel that way and say, “This is making me sell better.”


Identify the problem you need to solve, the same way I did with our brief. Pick the one thing that slips through the cracks on your busiest days and build your first prompt around it.


If you want more guidance, start with the[four levels of building Claude workflows](https://www.quo.com/blog/quo-claude-call-insights/) .
